spec.full_target: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer lambda with 0 <= lambda < p, and every admissible lattice M in the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2-module V(lambda), prove that M tensor_Z K is irreducible as the scalar-extension Lie algebra L(K)-module.
spec.conclusion: M tensor_Z K is irreducible as an L(K)-module, meaning it is nonzero and each K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is either zero or the whole space.

parameters.type: admissible lattice in V(lambda) over Z

hypotheses.statement: K is a field of characteristic p.
lambda is an integer and 0 <= lambda < p.

V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2-module of highest weight lambda, with generators x,y,h satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h and a nonzero highest-weight vector v with xv=0 and hv=lambda v; it has dimension lambda+1. M is any free abelian subgroup of V(lambda) whose Z-basis is a C-basis and for which U_Z M is contained in M, where U_Z is generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for integers r>=0.

calculations: Finite matrix multiplication, divided-power formulas obtained by iteration of the sl2 relations, localization and reduction of free modules, and explicit elementary ideal calculations in Z_(p).

primitives.meaning: Scalar extension of the Chevalley Z-form acting on M tensor K.

propositions.statement: K is a field of characteristic p.
lambda is an integer and 0 <= lambda < p.

V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2-module of highest weight lambda, with generators x,y,h satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h and a nonzero highest-weight vector v with xv=0 and hv=lambda v; it has dimension lambda+1. M is any free abelian subgroup of V(lambda) whose Z-basis is a C-basis and for which U_Z M is contained in M, where U_Z is generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for integers r>=0.
M tensor_Z K is irreducible as an L(K)-module, meaning it is nonzero and each K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is either zero or the whole space.

locals.declaration: Define M_R=R tensor_Z M embedded in V(lambda).
Define E_ab(e_b)=e_a and E_ab(e_t)=0 for t!=b.
Define E_i,j(e_j)=e_i and E_i,j(e_t)=0 for t!=j.
Define J_i={c in C:c e_i in M_R}.
Let J be the common J_i.
Choose generator a of rank-one free J using F001.

locals.type: image of a e_i in M_R/pM_R and its scalar extension to M tensor_Z K
locals.declaration: For each 0<=i<=lambda, define b_i as the image of a e_i under M_R -> M_R/pM_R and then under the canonical identification (M_R/pM_R) tensor_F_p K = M tensor_Z K.
Let W be any K-subspace invariant under x,y,h.

locals.type: prime subfield of K, canonically R/pR
locals.declaration: Let F_p be the prime subfield of K, canonically isomorphic to R/pR=Z/pZ.

argument.text: Let R=Z_(p), n=lambda+1, and e_i=y^i v/i! for 0<=i<=lambda. Iterating the given relations gives X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r), with an out-of-range e interpreted as zero. Thus these operators have integral matrices. Put M_R=R tensor_Z M inside V(lambda). Admissibility implies the R-algebra generated by all X_r,Y_r preserves M_R.

In the basis e_0,...,e_lambda let E_ab send e_b to e_a and the other basis vectors to zero. The displayed divided-power formulas give Y_lambda X_lambda=E_lambda,lambda; X_(lambda-i)E_lambda,lambda=E_i,lambda; and E_lambda,lambda Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_lambda,j. Since lambda<p, every binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R. Consequently every E_i,j belongs to the R-algebra generated by the divided powers and preserves M_R.

For each i set J_i={c in C: c e_i is in M_R}. The image E_i,i(M_R)=J_i e_i is finitely generated over R because M_R is finite free and an image of a finite module. It is nonzero: M_R spans V(lambda) over C and E_i,i is a nonzero projection. Since E_i,j preserves M_R, applying it to c e_j proves J_j subset J_i; reversing i,j proves equality. Denote the common module by J. Coordinate projections prove M_R=direct_sum_(i=0)^lambda J e_i. Tensoring with Q=Frac(R) and using rank_R(M_R)=n gives n=n rank_R(J), hence J has rank one. J is torsion-free as a submodule of C. A Q-linear identification Q tensor_R J=Q realizes J as a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of Q. Clear denominators to obtain a nonzero finitely generated ideal of R. Every nonzero q in Q is p^k u for an integer k and a unit u in R; among a finite set of nonzero ideal generators choose the least exponent k. Every generator is in p^k R and one is p^k times a unit, so the ideal is p^k R. Hence J is free of rank one. For a generator a of J, the vectors a e_i form an R-basis of M_R.

produces.statement: There exists a generator a of J and J is free of rank one over R.

argument.text: On the R-basis a e_0,...,a e_lambda established above, x(ae_i)=(lambda-i+1)ae_(i-1), y(ae_i)=(i+1)ae_(i+1), and h(ae_i)=(lambda-2i)ae_i, with out-of-range terms zero. Let F_p be the prime subfield of K, canonically isomorphic to R/pR=Z/pZ. The images of a e_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R because they are an R-basis of M_R. The natural map M_R/pM_R -> M tensor_Z F_p is an isomorphism: for a Z-basis of M, localization at integers prime to p reduces to the same F_p-basis. Extending scalars F_p -> K gives the K-basis b_0,...,b_lambda of M tensor_Z K, where b_i denotes the image of a e_i under these quotient and scalar-extension maps. These maps carry each integral action matrix to its reduction and then to K, so x b_i=(lambda-i+1)b_(i-1), y b_i=(i+1)b_(i+1), h b_i=(lambda-2i)b_i, with out-of-range terms zero. Thus this explicitly identifies the reduced representation and action; the characteristic-zero e_i are not vectors of M tensor_Z K.

For 0<=r<=lambda<p, r! is invertible modulo p, so the reductions of X_r and Y_r are scalar multiples of the corresponding powers of x and y on M tensor_Z K. The characteristic-zero identities defining E_i,j preserve M_R and their matrices in the R-basis a e_t are the usual matrix-unit matrices. Reduction modulo p and extension to K therefore give the matrix units in the explicitly defined basis b_0,...,b_lambda; equivalently the identities from S002 persist under these maps. Every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero modulo p because 0<=j<=lambda<p, hence is a unit in F_p and K. Thus any K-subspace W invariant under x and y is invariant under each reduced E_i,j. Write a nonzero w in W as w=sum_i c_i b_i and choose i with c_i nonzero. For every j, the reduced E_j,i sends w to c_i b_j, so b_j belongs to W because c_i is invertible in K. Hence W is the whole module. The basis has lambda+1 vectors, a positive integer, so the module is nonzero. This proves irreducibility, including lambda=0 and p=2.
